research_decisions.question: After verifying Peng 2026 from the original, does the manuscript's Section 5 contribution (a five-decision sensitivity ranking with fit scope and evaluation population dominant) survive as an IEEE TIM contribution?
research_decisions.decision: NO-GO for IEEE TIM in the present framing. Reposition the manuscript as a bounded empirical study of estimator- and population-dependence in fixed-budget donor allocation; withdraw the Section 5 dominance ranking and interaction claims pending correction. Correct Reference 5's fabricated title.
research_decisions.rationale: Codex returned NO-GO and, independently, identified implementation defects in the sensitivity scripts. I read budget.py, joint.py, strat.py and isu_budget.py and confirmed every structural claim: the 'fit scope' factor is not implemented as a scope change, the 'row allocation' factor is mathematically inactive at K=8, the interaction has no inferential test, and the two sections use different quartile definitions.
evidence: Original Peng 2026 PDF (29 pp, .research/peng2026/peng2026.txt): real title is 'Deployable Self-Referenced Features for Cross-Cell Battery State-of-Health Estimation: Randomized Pairing Controls and Benchmarking'; the manuscript's Reference 5 title is fabricated
Peng 2026 full text: 'interaction' 0 hits, 'dominance'/'dominat' 0 hits, 'multiverse' 0 hits; but Peng DOES run a 2x2 factorial (feature richness x normalization), contradicting manuscript line 37
Peng 2026 numbers verified verbatim: 108% (max +107.8%), -5.3%->+4.5%, offline -16.8%/-19.1% -> strict online +4.3%/+10.4%
.research/results/budget.py:60-65 and isu_budget.py:57-62: scope=='condition' branch uses ALL donor rows (not 8), bypasses the NDRAW loop, and fits per evaluated cell - not a shared per-condition fit
.research/results/budget.py:69-73 and isu_budget.py:66-70: exact and floor(k/m) allocate identical rows for K=8, m in {1,2} - the row-allocation factor is a null operation measuring only RNG drift
.research/results/budget.py:53-59 and isu_budget.py:50-56: eligibility via len(donors)<m differs between arms, so evaluated cell sets differ
.research/results/joint.py:98-99: interaction computed from four aggregate deltas with no condition-level interval or test
.research/results/strat.py:44 uses global RUL quartiles; budget.py:48-50 and isu_budget.py:47-53 use condition-specific quartiles - different populations
rejected_options: Keep the five-decision ranking as the lead contribution (rejected: the leading factor is mislabelled and one factor is inactive)
Lead with the 2x2 interaction test (rejected: no condition-level test, and Peng already uses a factorial)
Lead with ranking instability across datasets (rejected: ordering change is a boundary, not a contribution)
scientific_risks: The 'evaluation population reverses sign on both datasets' claim may survive, but it is a condition-specific quartile in Section 5 and a global quartile in Section 4.3
The null row-allocation factor suggests the Monte-Carlo noise floor is 10-28% of the contrast, which shrinks the apparent effect of the other two 'small' decisions
Repositioning may leave no TIM-level contribution at all, requiring a venue change

falsification_criteria: If a corrected scope implementation (one shared affine fit per condition, exactly 8 rows, common evaluated cells) reproduces the +274%/+140% scope dominance, the ranking claim is restored
If the late-life sign reversal disappears when all-query and late-life summaries reuse the same calibrated predictions on common support, withdraw it as the replicated population result
If the null row-allocation factor turns out to be a coding slip rather than a design feature, the 'five decisions' framing can be restored with four
